title: Lyaadh
description: Bengali for the art of pleasurable lethargy. A brand I'm building slowly and honestly — in revival after a real outage, one published piece so far, and the actual product (a slow, anti-productivity browser game) still at the concept-picking stage. Built with my partner, who owns the writing.
lede: Bengali for the art of pleasurable lethargy. I wanted to build something slower — including the pace I build it at.
story:
Lyaadh is a Bengali word with no clean English translation — the feeling of lying around on a Sunday afternoon not because you're tired, but because you've decided the world can wait. My family uses it. It's not an apology for doing nothing; it's a chosen state.

The honest version of where this stands: it's early. The domain's been live since April, the brand identity is settled (deep green, ochre, cream; "the guilt-free enjoyment of non-doing"), and there's one published piece — a Koh Lanta "lyaadh escape" article. In August the site went down for a while — an expired TLS cert plus a crashed process pointing at a directory that no longer existed — and coming back from that turned into an opportunity: instead of restoring the old database, Lyaadh's content now runs on the same CMS infrastructure I built for Roami, as its first real tenant outside WanderingBong.

The actual product — a slow, anti-productivity browser game — is still at the idea stage. Four mechanics are on the table: an anti-clicker that rewards not interacting, a post-lunch nap simulator, an "adda" conversation game about going nowhere in particular, and a waiting room where nothing happens on purpose. I haven't picked one yet. Whichever it is will be browser-only, no account, no server state, and kept off the live site until it's actually worth showing.

The lane split is the part I like most: my partner owns the writing and cultural voice, I own the product and the build. Different instincts, and the brand is better for it.
